title: Rigveda 8.14: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.14: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.14 is a hymn of 15 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 583r-584r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.14.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 1, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 583r
translation.original_text:
1yad i̍ndrā̱haṁ yathā̱ tvam īśī̍ya̱ vasva̱ eka̱ it | sto̱tā me̱ goṣa̍khā syāt ||
2śikṣe̍yam asmai̱ ditse̍ya̱ṁ śacī̍pate manī̱ṣiṇe̍ | yad a̱haṁ gopa̍ti̱ḥ syām ||
3dhe̱nuṣ ṭa̍ indra sū̱nṛtā̱ yaja̍mānāya sunva̱te | gām aśva̍m pi̱pyuṣī̍ duhe ||
4na te̍ va̱rtāsti̱ rādha̍sa̱ indra̍ de̱vo na martya̍ḥ | yad ditsa̍si stu̱to ma̱gham ||
translation.text:
1IF I, O Indra, were, like thee, the single Sovran of all wealth, My worshipper should be rich in kine.
2I should be fain, O Lord of Power, to strengthen and enrich the sage, Were I the Lord of herds of kine.
3To worshippers who press the juice thy goodness, Indra, is a cow Yielding in plenty kine and steeds.
4None is there, Indra, God or man, to hinder thy munificence, The wealth which, lauded, thou wilt give.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 583r (numbered 5r by the scribe) (OPenn image 583, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.13.27 ‹-svara›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 583v (numbered 5v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.14.5 ‹-bhūmim vi avartayat cakrāṇaḥ›. Verses 8.14.1-4 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 8.14.5-14 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 1, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 583v
translation.original_text:
5ya̱jña indra̍m avardhaya̱d yad bhūmi̱ṁ vy ava̍rtayat | ca̱krā̱ṇa o̍pa̱śaṁ di̱vi ||
6vā̱vṛ̱dhā̱nasya̍ te va̱yaṁ viśvā̱ dhanā̍ni ji̱gyuṣa̍ḥ | ū̱tim i̱ndrā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
7vy a1̱̍ntari̍kṣam atira̱n made̱ soma̍sya roca̱nā | indro̱ yad abhi̍nad va̱lam ||
8ud gā ā̍ja̱d aṅgi̍robhya ā̱viṣ kṛ̱ṇvan guhā̍ sa̱tīḥ | a̱rvāñca̍ṁ nunude va̱lam ||
9indre̍ṇa roca̱nā di̱vo dṛ̱ḻhāni̍ dṛṁhi̱tāni̍ ca | sthi̱rāṇi̱ na pa̍rā̱ṇude̍ ||
10a̱pām ū̱rmir mada̍nn iva̱ stoma̍ indrājirāyate | vi te̱ madā̍ arājiṣuḥ ||
11tvaṁ hi sto̍ma̱vardha̍na̱ indrāsy u̍ktha̱vardha̍naḥ | sto̱tṝ̱ṇām u̱ta bha̍dra̱kṛt ||
12indra̱m it ke̱śinā̱ harī̍ soma̱peyā̍ya vakṣataḥ | upa̍ ya̱jñaṁ su̱rādha̍sam ||
13a̱pām phene̍na̱ namu̍ce̱ḥ śira̍ i̱ndrod a̍vartayaḥ | viśvā̱ yad aja̍ya̱ḥ spṛdha̍ḥ ||
14mā̱yābhi̍r u̱tsisṛ̍psata̱ indra̱ dyām ā̱ruru̍kṣataḥ | ava̱ dasyū̍m̐r adhūnuthāḥ ||
translation.text:
5The sacrifice made Indra strong when he unrolled the earth, and made Himself a diadem in heaven.
6Thine aid we claim, O Indra, thine who after thou hast waxen great Hast won all treasures for thine own.
7In Soma's ecstasy Indra spread the firmament and realms of light, When he cleft Vala limb from limb.
8Showing the hidden he drave forth the cows for the Angirases, And Vala he cast headlong down.
9By Indra were the luminous realms of heaven established and secured, Firm and immovable from their place.
10Indra, thy laud moves quickly like a joyous wave of water-floods: Bright shine the drops that gladden thee.
11For thou, O Indra, art the God whom hymns and praises magnify: Thou blessest those who worship thee.
12Let the two long-maned Bay Steeds bring Indra to drink the Soma juice, The Bountiful to our sacrifice.
13With waters' foam thou torest off, Indra, the head of Namuci, Subduing all contending hosts.
14The Dasyus, when they fain would climb by magic arts and mount to heaven, Thou, Indra, castest down to earth.

translation.text: <sup>15</sup>As Soma-drinker conquering all, thou scatteredst to every side Their settlement who poured no gifts.
